entries.title: Vaults on USB flash drives
entries.description: A vault can now live on a USB flash drive plugged into your phone, created here or opened from one made elsewhere, and a drive prepared here opens in desktop VeraCrypt. Give the vault a partition and the rest of the drive stays ordinary storage - the create wizard has a partition editor for it. Two things are worth knowing before you rely on one: a drive whose whole surface is a vault has no partition table, so Android offers to format it on every connection and accepting that destroys the vault; and pulling a drive without ejecting can lose the last writes, so use Eject and wait for the confirmation. Full details, including what Arcanum does not do about counterfeit drives, are at arcanum.zip/docs/usb-drives (#95) (#131)

entries.title: Coming back to Arcanum asks for the PIN again
entries.description: Android shuts apps down in the background to reclaim memory, and some phones do it eagerly. When that happened to Arcanum it came back on the screen you had left it on, already past the calculator, because the app that had been unlocked was gone and the one that took its place had no way to tell. The unlock now belongs to the running app rather than to the screen, so anything that shuts Arcanum down means entering the PIN again. On a phone that is aggressive about background apps you will meet the calculator more often than before, whatever the auto-lock delay is set to. (#150)

entries.title: A photo keeps the place it was taken
entries.description: A photo carries the place it was taken inside it, and Android strips that out before handing the file to an app that has not been allowed to see it. A photo put into a vault lost its location silently, and for good if you had also asked for the original to be deleted. Arcanum now asks for that permission the first time you import something, after explaining what is about to be asked and why - the system dialog speaks of access to photos and videos, which sounds far broader than what it actually grants. Declining is fine: the import works either way, and only the location is lost. Files arriving through Share go through the same check. (#149)

entries.title: Imported files keep their own date
entries.description: Until now everything imported into a FAT or exFAT vault was stamped 1 January 2025 - one fixed date for every file, because the vault had no clock to ask. It has one now, and more than that: a file keeps the date it already had, so a vault sorted by date comes out in the order you expect. This applies to what you import from here on. Files already inside a vault keep the date they were given, because their original date is not recorded anywhere to put back. Going the other way, a file exported out of a vault still carries the date it was exported: Android does not let an app set timestamps in shared storage without a broad storage permission, and Arcanum does not ask for one. (#154)

entries.title: Sorting and filtering the Gallery
entries.description: The Gallery can be sorted now: by name, date, size, type, or at random. There is a view options button in its top bar, and the All / Photos / Videos filter moved in there with it, which gives the grid back the row the filter chips used to occupy. Your choice is remembered. The month and day headers stay for the date order, where a timeline is what they describe, and step out of the way for the others. The random order reshuffles each time you come back to the Gallery, which is a good way to meet a collection you had forgotten the middle of. (#122) (#151)

entries.title: Swiping follows the order you chose
entries.description: Opening a photo and swiping sideways used to walk through files in the order the vault happened to index them, whatever sorting you had picked in the list you opened them from. It now follows that list: the Files browser's order when you open from Files, the Gallery's when you open from the Gallery. (#151)

entries.title: Pinch to zoom a video
entries.description: A video can be pinched to zoom and dragged around, the way photos already could. Double tap still seeks ten seconds, and the fullscreen button still turns the screen for videos wider than they are tall. (#151)

entries.title: A long operation no longer locks the app in the middle of itself
entries.description: Auto-lock measured how long it had been since you last touched the screen, and watching a progress bar is not a touch. A vault that took longer to open than the auto-lock delay therefore threw you back to the calculator part way through opening it - and with "unmount on auto-lock" switched on, it tore down the volume it was still setting up. The timer now counts the app working for you as well as your touches: opening a vault, creating one, changing a password or a keyfile, backing up or restoring a header, a long import and playing a video all hold the lock open while they run, and the delay starts counting from the moment the work stops rather than from your last touch before it. Leaving the app in the middle of an operation now waits for it to finish instead of cutting it short. A vault does stay unlocked for as long as an operation runs, which is the deliberate half of the trade.

entries.title: A vault does not close itself while it is busy
entries.description: Copying a large folder into a vault and then putting the phone down used to be enough to lose the rest of it: switching away, or letting the screen turn off, closed the vault if you had asked it to close on either, and whatever was still being written stopped where it was. Both of those settings now wait for the work to finish before they close anything, and if you come back before it does, the vault simply stays open. Only unmounting a vault yourself, or the panic PIN, stops an operation part way. The vault is still flushed to disk the moment you switch away, so nothing has to wait for the work to finish to be safe.

entries.title: Choosing a file no longer locks the app
entries.description: Picking files or a folder to import means leaving Arcanum for the system's own file picker, and the minutes spent there counted as time doing nothing at all. On a short auto-lock delay, looking for the right folder was enough to come back to the PIN screen - and the import would then run anyway, behind it, with nothing on screen to say so. Time spent in a picker Arcanum opened is no longer idle time, and a result arriving after the app has locked is refused rather than quietly written into a vault you have been told is closed. A picker left open for more than fifteen minutes stops holding the vault open, on the grounds that nobody spends that long choosing a file.

entries.title: Importing over a file that already exists asks first
entries.description: Importing a file whose name was already taken in the destination wrote straight over it - no question, no copy kept, and nothing to undo it with. Copying inside a vault has always made a numbered duplicate instead, so the same app treated the same collision two different ways and the silent one was the one that destroyed something. Arcanum now stops at the first name that clashes and asks: keep both, skip it, or replace it. The answer covers the rest of that import, which the question says plainly - a folder of a thousand files should not mean a thousand taps. A folder whose name already exists still merges into the one that is there, the way it always did, and the summary at the end says how many files were left alone. (#157)

entries.title: A vault remembers how it was opened
entries.description: The options on the unlock screen were forgotten the moment you left it. Read-only did not survive even turning the phone, and unlocking with a fingerprint - which shows no options at all - fell back to the defaults every time: a vault you had opened read-only came back writable, and every unlock paid again for working out which hash the vault uses, which can be the difference between one second and eight. A vault now remembers what its last successful unlock used, and a fingerprint unlock opens it the same way. The hash and cipher are taken from the vault itself rather than from what was typed, so this makes unlocking quicker even if you never touched those settings. Your password, PIM and keyfiles are unchanged in where they live: still only in the fingerprint store, never beside the vault. (#148)

entries.title: Dialogs have a background in AMOLED mode
entries.description: In AMOLED mode a few dialogs and sheets drew with nothing behind them at all. The confirmation for turning off biometric unlock was see-through, and so were the ones on the change password and change keyfile screens. All of them sit on a proper surface now.

entries.title: ext4 vaults are much faster to fill
entries.description: Adding files to an ext4 vault wrote about twice as much to storage as the files themselves, because the bookkeeping was redone for every single block. It happens once per run of blocks now, so a large import writes about half as much and finishes noticeably sooner. (#155) (#160) (#161) (#162)

entries.title: Deleting from an ext4 vault is much lighter on storage
entries.description: Removing a file from an ext4 vault rewrote a block of bookkeeping once for every block the file held, so deleting a large file wrote about as much to storage as adding it did. It happens once per run of blocks now: on a phone, clearing twelve files out of a vault took 159 writes, where deleting a single one of them used to take about five thousand. (#165)

entries.title: Links made on a computer are shown as links
entries.description: A shortcut made on a computer - what Linux calls a symlink - appeared in an ext4 vault as a tiny damaged file that would not open, and exporting one could hand you a text file containing a path where the real file should have been. They are now shown as links: a link to a file opens the file, a link to a folder goes into the folder, and one pointing at something that is not in the vault says so instead of failing silently. Links written on a computer very often point outside the vault, and there is nothing there to reach - so those are marked rather than left looking broken. (#163)

entries.title: The same file in two places, without a second copy
entries.description: A file can now be given a second name somewhere else in the same ext4 vault: three dots on it, Create link, then pick the folder. It is not a copy and not a shortcut - it is the same file, so it takes no extra space, changes to it show in both places, and removing one of the names leaves the other working. Its properties say how many places it is in, and deleting it says so too rather than claiming the file is gone for good. A folder can be linked the same way, though a folder link is a pointer rather than the folder itself, so it stops working if the folder is moved or removed. ext4 vaults only: FAT and exFAT have no such thing, and the entry does not appear there. (#128)

entries.title: Exporting a link says what could not leave the vault
entries.description: Outside a vault there is no such thing as a second name for a file, so a link cannot leave as a link - but export used to answer that badly. A link to a folder was written out as an empty file under the folder's name, and so was a link pointing at something that is not in the vault; both were then counted as exported, so the summary said an item had left while what landed outside held nothing. A folder link now leaves as a real copy of the folder it points at, under its own name. A link that leads nowhere is skipped and counted rather than written out empty, and so is a folder link that points back into what is being exported. And when two of the names you exported turn out to be the same file, the summary says so, because outside the vault they are two separate copies taking the space twice. (#167)

entries.title: Copying or moving a link keeps it a link
entries.description: Copying a link to a folder, or one pointing at something that is no longer in the vault, used to produce a file of zero bytes under the link's name - and if you had cut it rather than copied it, the link itself was deleted afterwards, so what you moved was gone and what arrived was empty. A link is now copied as a link, keeping the same target, dead ones included. Moving anything inside a vault has also become a plain rename: nothing is read or written, so it is instant however large the file is, and a file that has two names keeps both - moving one of them used to quietly make a second separate file holding its own copy. Into another vault, or onto a FAT one, a link cannot be a link at all: copying it takes a copy of what it leads to, and moving it leaves it where it is rather than turning it into a copy, with the summary saying how many items stayed behind. (#168)

entries.title: Pasting over something that already exists asks first
entries.description: Importing a file whose name was already taken asks what to do - keep both, skip, or replace. Pasting did not ask at all: it wrote straight over whatever held the name, with nothing said before or after, and a folder pasted onto a folder of the same name overwrote the files inside it that clashed, equally silently. The same question is now asked by Paste, by Copy to and Move to, and by the files inside a folder they merge into, with one answer covering the rest of that operation. A folder itself is still not asked about, because it merges into the one that is there rather than replacing it, and copying something into the folder it already lives in still makes a numbered duplicate without asking. (#169)

entries.title: An export that could not read a file says so
entries.description: If a file could not be read to the end - a damaged vault, a drive pulled mid-export - what had already been written was left outside under the file's own name and counted as exported. Nothing about a half-written file looks half-written, so the summary said the export had gone through and what you had was part of a photo. What did come out is now kept rather than deleted, because an export is how a vault in trouble is rescued, but it is named with .part on the end so it cannot be taken for the whole file, and the summary says how many came out that way instead of showing a tick. (#170)

entries.title: An interrupted write no longer damages a file that was already there
entries.description: If the app is killed, the battery runs out or a drive is pulled while a file is being added to an ext4 vault, losing what was still being written is expected. Losing part of what the file already held is not, and it could happen - a filesystem check settled the interruption by throwing away the file's newest piece, and that piece could include data written before the operation started. The vault's bookkeeping is now written in an order that makes a check settle it the other way, and put the vault right on its own. (#164)

entries.title: A badly fragmented ext4 vault keeps taking files
entries.description: In an ext4 vault fragmented enough that one file needed thousands of separate pieces - the state a vault reaches after being filled, emptied and refilled many times - a write could be refused as though the vault were full while there was still room in it. The map that records where a file's pieces are had a ceiling it could not grow past. It grows now, the way a Linux ext4 driver does, so what stops a write is running out of space and nothing else. Nothing changed on disk: existing vaults are unaffected, and one grown this way still mounts on a Linux desktop. (#119)

entries.title: An ext4 vault made on a computer can be filled to the end
entries.description: A vault formatted as ext4 anywhere other than Arcanum - mkfs.ext4 on a Linux desktop, say - refused writes as though it were full while most of it was still empty. On a 260 MB vault it gave up after 76 MB. Formatting a volume leaves the bookkeeping for most of it unwritten, on the understanding that whichever driver first needs the space will fill that part in; Arcanum skipped those parts instead, so everything they covered was out of reach. It fills them in now, the way a Linux ext4 driver does, and the same applied to the record of which files exist, so creating files in such a vault stopped early too. Vaults created by Arcanum were never affected, and nothing about the on-disk format changes: a vault written this way still mounts on a Linux desktop. (#140)

entries.title: Folders of an ext4 vault made on a computer accept new files
entries.description: A folder that a desktop let grow past a certain size gets a hidden index to speed up name lookups, and Arcanum would not write into one: adding or renaming anything inside it failed, and on a vault made with mkfs.ext4 that was most of the folders with a lot in them. Such a folder is now rebuilt as an ordinary one the first time something is written to it, which takes a moment on a very large folder and happens once. The folder keeps everything in it and still opens on a Linux desktop; only the index is gone, and the desktop's own e2fsck -D puts it back if it is wanted. (#141)

entries.title: An ext4 vault says when it was interrupted
entries.description: If the app is killed, the battery runs out or a drive is pulled while a file is being written, an ext4 vault is now marked as unfinished, and opening it tells you so once. Nothing is lost and the vault works normally - what is left behind is bookkeeping a filesystem check tidies up, which every write of every operation was interrupted on purpose to establish. A Linux desktop opening the same container sees the same mark and runs its own check without being asked. arcanum.zip/docs/filesystems explains what is and is not promised. (#142)

entries.title: The path above the file list is no longer see-through
entries.description: In the ordinary theme the row of folder names above a vault's contents had no background of its own, so the list scrolled visibly through it. It now takes the colour of the bar it sits under. In AMOLED mode, where it stands on frosted glass, nothing changes.

entries.title: The import indicator says how far along it is
entries.description: Importing showed a bar that moved on its own and told you nothing: not how much of the file had been written, and not how many files were left. It now names the file being imported and fills the bar as the bytes land - with the percentage beside it when you imported one file, and which of them this is, 3/7, when you imported several. A file whose size the source will not report still gets the old running bar, since a made-up position is worse than none.

entries.title: Unlocking a vault is a button now
entries.description: Nothing on the unlock screen said how to actually unlock: the only way in was the enter key on the keyboard, which one person reported spending ten minutes looking for. The large lock is the button now - tap it and the vault opens. It shifts gently every few seconds so it reads as something to press, and tapping it with nothing filled in shakes and says what is missing instead of doing nothing at all. The vault's icon above it opens the details of a mounted vault, and the separate row and toolbar icon that used to carry these two jobs are gone. (#120)

entries.title: Remove from list is now Forget, and it asks first
entries.description: Taking a vault off the list was called Remove, wore a bin icon and happened on a single tap, with nothing said about what that meant. In selection mode it was worse: the same bin removed entries and never touched a file. It is called Forget now, it asks first, and the confirmation says plainly what goes and what stays - the entry and its thumbnails go, the vault file itself is left exactly where it is. Forget also sits in a vault's own menu, not only in selection mode.

entries.title: Forgetting a vault clears its media index as well
entries.description: Removing a vault from the list used to leave rows behind in the app's own media index: the names and paths of files that had been inside that vault, kept on the device after the vault was gone from the list. They are deleted along with the vault now, as its thumbnails already were.

entries.title: Links in these notes are tappable
entries.description: Addresses written in What's New entries, like the documentation links above, can be tapped instead of copied out by hand.

entries.title: Adding a vault starts in a folder, not in Recent
entries.description: Choosing Internal storage when adding an existing vault opened the system picker on Recent, which is usually empty for a vault file - leaving you to find the picker's own folder drawer before you could look anywhere. It now opens at the folder of a vault you already added, or at internal storage if this is your first. The picker is the system's own screen, so this is a hint rather than a guarantee, but where it is honoured it saves the detour. (#126)

entries.title: The calculator works turned sideways
entries.description: Rotating the phone left the calculator unusable: its buttons are circles sized from the width of the screen, so in landscape a row of four was as tall as a quarter of the screen is wide and the bottom three rows sat off the edge, digits included. Landscape now puts the display beside the keypad instead of above it, and the buttons are sized by whichever way the screen runs out first. This is also how it looks on a tablet, where sideways is the usual way round. (#124)

entries.title: The filesystem step recommends the right one, and keeps your choice
entries.description: The create wizard marked FAT as recommended for every vault it could make: the size above which it was meant to suggest exFAT had been set to two terabytes. It is now 4 GB, which is the number that makes the choice mean anything - a vault smaller than that cannot hold a file FAT would refuse, so exFAT gains nothing there and costs compatibility. Picking a filesystem by hand also sticks now: stepping back to change the size and returning replaced your choice with the recommendation, quietly, which was easy to miss on the way to creating the vault.

entries.title: No crash when a large file is picked as a keyfile
entries.description: Choosing a big file as a keyfile - a video, a disk image, anything past roughly a hundred megabytes - closed the app on the spot, with no message and nothing written down. The whole file was being loaded into memory even though only its first megabyte can ever matter: that is all VeraCrypt mixes into the password, and everything after it is ignored by every implementation. Arcanum now reads only that first megabyte, and reads it off the main thread, so a keyfile kept in a cloud or network folder no longer freezes the screen while it downloads either. Vaults and keyfiles are unaffected - the bytes that reach the volume are identical. (#136)

entries.title: Copy, Move and Paste say what they did
entries.description: With one vault open, Copy and Move put the files on a clipboard and the only sign of it was a Paste entry appearing inside the menu at the top - nothing on screen said the copy had landed, so the buttons looked broken. Both now confirm how many items are waiting and where to paste them from. A paste reports its result too: how many arrived, how many failed, and when it correctly did nothing because the files were already in that folder. A failed paste used to look exactly like a successful one. (#129)

entries.title: The video menu no longer closes by itself
entries.description: Opening the three-dot menu over a video and taking a moment to read it meant losing it: the menu belongs to the player's top bar, and the bar hides itself three seconds after it appears, taking the menu down with it. The bar now stays put while the menu is open, and starts its countdown again once the menu is closed. (#138)

entries.title: Create vaults as ext4
entries.description: Vaults can now be formatted as ext4, alongside FAT and exFAT, from the format step when you create one. ext4 does away with FAT's limits - there is no cap on how many files a folder holds, and it fragments far less as a vault fills - and it is a real Linux filesystem, so a vault made here mounts read-write on a Linux desktop with the standard tools, and an ext4 container made on a desktop opens here. It is not readable on Windows or macOS without a separate ext4 driver, so pick ext4 if you work on Linux or stay on the phone, and keep FAT or exFAT for the widest desktop reach. The ext4 support is a clean-room implementation written from the published on-disk format, carrying no third-party filesystem code. (#7)

entries.title: Correct location for vaults added from the Downloads or Videos picker
entries.description: Adding an existing vault while the file picker was showing Downloads, Videos, or any section other than the device's own storage showed a meaningless location like Internal/1000000123 instead of the real folder. The vault's location now resolves correctly no matter which picker section you chose the file from.

entries.title: Open FAT32 vaults created by other apps
entries.description: Some apps (for example AndroidCrypt) format small containers as FAT32 even when they hold too few clusters to qualify as FAT32 under the spec. Arcanum's bundled filesystem rejected these with a mount failure, even though the password was correct and the same vault opened fine in desktop VeraCrypt. Arcanum now honors the on-disk FAT32 layout and mounts these vaults.

entries.title: Clear message when a storage location is read-only
entries.description: Some storage providers, such as certain network or SMB shares, let an app read a vault file but not write to it. Mounting such a vault read-write failed with a generic error. Arcanum now recognizes this and shows a clear message that the location is read-only and to mount it read-only instead, rather than an unhelpful failure, and read-only mounts of the same vaults keep working.

entries.title: Save the last mount log for bug reports
entries.description: Debug mode can now keep the log of the most recent mount so it can be shared when something goes wrong. Turn on Save last mount log in Settings > Debug, reproduce the mount, then copy the saved log from the same screen. Previously the mount log was visible only live during mounting and could not be captured.

entries.title: No crash playing media on 32-bit devices
entries.description: On 32-bit ARM devices, playing an audio or video file from a vault could crash the app. Decryption performed unaligned 64-bit memory accesses that 32-bit CPUs reject, triggered when playback read from a position that was not sector-aligned. Reads are now aligned before decryption, so media plays without crashing. (#92)

entries.title: Hardened biometric app unlock
entries.description: The fingerprint prompt that unlocks the app is now tied to a hardware-backed Keystore operation, so only a genuine biometric match can pass it. Before, the unlock relied on the prompt's success signal alone, which on a rooted or instrumented device could be driven directly to reveal the vault list (each vault stayed separately encrypted, so no vault contents were exposed). App unlock now works the same way per-vault unlock already did. (#89)

entries.title: Generate keyfiles in the app
entries.description: Keyfiles can now be created inside Arcanum instead of having to bring your own file. Pick Generate keyfile from the + button on the vault list for the full options - how many, what size, and extra randomness collected from your touch - or use Generate new keyfile right in the keyfile step while creating a vault or changing its keyfiles. Files are filled with cryptographically secure random data and stay interchangeable with desktop VeraCrypt. A keyfile is only its exact bytes, so back it up like a password: lose it and the vault is gone. (#110)

entries.title: Keyfile vaults with very long passwords now match VeraCrypt
entries.description: When a keyfile was combined with a password longer than 64 bytes, Arcanum mixed them differently than VeraCrypt does. A vault created here that way could not be opened in desktop VeraCrypt, and VeraCrypt vaults created that way could not be opened here. The limit counts bytes rather than characters, so a password in a non-Latin alphabet crossed it at around 33 characters. Arcanum now matches VeraCrypt exactly. Vaults made by earlier versions still open - Arcanum detects the old format and retries automatically - and changing the password, or backing up, restoring or expanding such a vault, rewrites it in the correct format. Note that vaults created from now on with a keyfile and a password this long will not open in Arcanum versions older than this one. (#112)

entries.title: Moving a file or folder to where it already is no longer deletes it
entries.description: Selecting Move on an item and then pasting it into the same folder made it disappear. Arcanum copied the item onto itself and then removed the original, so nothing was left. Pasting an item into the folder it already sits in now simply does nothing, and pasting a folder into itself or into one of its own subfolders is refused instead of destroying it. Copying an item into its own folder now makes a numbered duplicate, the way other file managers do. (#113)

entries.title: Rename folders, not just files
entries.description: Folders can now be renamed: the same menu that files have is available on folder rows, with Rename and Properties. Previously there was no way to rename a folder at all, which is what led to the move-and-lose-it problem above. A folder with a dot in its name, such as photos.2026, is also handled correctly now - the full name is shown when renaming, and nothing is appended afterwards. (#113)

entries.title: Import errors now say what actually went wrong
entries.description: Every failed import claimed "Not enough space in the vault" no matter the cause, and a vault that genuinely was full was not even recognised as such - so the one problem the message named was the one it could never detect. Imports now report the real reason. One case worth knowing about: the top level of a vault formatted as FAT can hold a limited number of entries, fixed when the vault is created, and long filenames use up several each - so it can fill up after a hundred or so files while the vault itself is nearly empty. Arcanum now says so and points you at a subfolder, which has no such limit. Apps writing into a mounted vault from outside also get a proper out-of-space error instead of a generic failure. (#114)

entries.title: New vaults hold far more files at the top level
entries.description: Vaults were being formatted in a way that capped the top level at a few hundred files, no matter how much room was left inside - after that, importing failed however small the file was. New vaults are now formatted the way desktop VeraCrypt does it, so the top level grows as needed and that limit is gone. Space is used more efficiently too: small files waste much less room than before. This applies to vaults created from now on. Existing vaults keep the old layout, so if you have hit the limit in one, moving files into subfolders will get you going again, or recreate the vault to be rid of it. (#115)

entries.title: Rename and Properties from the grid layout
entries.description: The grid layout offered no actions on individual items, so renaming was possible only in the list layout. Press and hold an item to select it and Rename and Properties now appear at the top, in either layout.

entries.title: Keyfiles never touch storage any more
entries.description: Whenever you used a keyfile - creating a vault, changing a password or keyfile, backing up or restoring a header, expanding a vault - Arcanum first copied it into its own cache folder unencrypted, and relied on deleting it afterwards. That copy is gone: keyfiles are now read straight into memory, used, and wiped, exactly as they already were when mounting. Unlocking a vault was never affected. (#116)

entries.title: Interface polish
entries.description: Progress and completion screens now look and behave the same everywhere - a few of them were missing their animation or their haptic entirely, which made a long operation look like a stalled one. What's New groups entries by kind, new features first and fixes last, rather than listing them in the order they happened to be written. And the password steps no longer leave an empty band of background sitting above the keyboard.

entries.title: Video thumbnails that actually show something
entries.description: A video's thumbnail was always its very first frame, so anything opening on black, on a white slate, or on a plain title card showed up in the gallery as an empty square - and every such video looked identical. Arcanum now uses the cover image stored in the file when there is one, and otherwise checks whether the first frame is a solid fill and reaches a little further into the video when it is. Videos that already had a usable first frame keep it. Existing thumbnails are regenerated once, the next time you open the gallery. (#111)

entries.title: Open a file in another app without decrypting it to disk
entries.description: Open with is now an item in each file's menu, and it no longer works by writing a decrypted copy into the cache first. The other app is handed the file straight out of the mounted vault instead, so nothing plaintext ever reaches storage, and a large video opens immediately rather than after a long wait - it used to be read into memory in full, which could fail outright on a big file. Because this route exposes the vault to the other app, it asks first if External app access is off for that vault, and you can turn it back off in the vault's settings. Any decrypted copies left behind by the old version are wiped the next time you open a vault. (#103)

entries.title: Storage no longer shows free space that isn't there
entries.description: The Storage screen took a vault's size from the volume header rather than from the filesystem inside it. Those are the same number until a vault is expanded, after which the header grows but the filesystem does not - so an expanded vault could report gigabytes free while refusing to accept a single file. Sizes now come from the filesystem, and where a vault's volume is larger than the filesystem in it, the screen says so instead of leaving two screens quietly disagreeing.

entries.title: Expand Volume has been removed
entries.description: Expanding grew the encrypted container but not the filesystem inside it, and neither Arcanum nor desktop VeraCrypt can grow a FAT or exFAT filesystem - VeraCrypt warns about exactly this before expanding, and only finishes the job for NTFS, which Arcanum does not use. The added space was therefore never usable on the phone, so the action has been withdrawn rather than left looking like it worked. To get more room, create a larger vault and move your files into it, or expand the container on a desktop and extend the filesystem there. Vaults expanded by an earlier version are unaffected and keep working.

entries.title: Clean icons in the storage chart
entries.description: The icons drifting through the ring on a vault's Storage screen were drawn with visible streaks and distortion, and some came out looking nothing like the icon they were meant to be. They are now drawn from a single crisp copy of each icon, and they are also kept clear of the edges of their slice, so a thin slice no longer trims them down to a sliver.

entries.title: Donations
entries.description: Support the project in Settings now opens a screen of its own, with GitHub Sponsors and Ko-fi alongside addresses for Bitcoin, Lightning, Ethereum, Monero and Solana - tap one to copy it. Nothing is sent anywhere: the app has no network access, so a payment is always finished in your own wallet or browser. (#66)

entries.title: Runs on devices with 16 KB memory pages
entries.description: The encrypted-database library shipped with Arcanum was built for 4 KB memory pages. On a device using the 16 KB page size that newer Android versions support, it could not be loaded at all, and the app died on startup as soon as it touched its database. It has been replaced with a build that handles both. Your data is untouched - the database format is identical and existing vaults open as before. (#45)

entries.title: Smoother playback progress
entries.description: The video seek bar and the audio waveform advanced in five visible steps a second, because that is how often playback position was sampled. Both now move continuously.

entries.title: Fullscreen video
entries.description: A video wider than it is tall now has a fullscreen button in its own corner. Tapping it turns the screen so the video fills it, carrying on from the same moment, and the way back sits next to the timecode. Videos shot upright already fill the screen, so they do not offer it. Double-tap seeking got tidier too: the -10s and +10s markers now appear over the video rather than below it, a double tap no longer pulls the controls up when they are hidden, and it keeps them up when they are not.

entries.title: Storage figures keep up with changes
entries.description: The Storage screen worked its numbers out once and then held them, so importing or deleting files left it showing the old breakdown until the vault was unmounted and mounted again. It now updates as files change, and recounts whenever the tab is opened.

entries.title: Album art for music files
entries.description: Music files in the file browser now show their embedded cover art instead of a generic icon, in both the list and grid layouts. Tracks without artwork keep the icon. Opus files are also counted as music on the Storage screen now, rather than as ordinary files.

entries.title: Music files are marked as music
entries.description: A track showing its cover art now carries a small note over it, the way a video carries a play triangle, so artwork is not mistaken for a photo at a glance.

entries.title: Calculator disguise shows at launch
entries.description: With the calculator disguise enabled, a cold start sometimes showed the PIN screen instead of the calculator. The lock screen now waits for the disguise setting to load before choosing, so the calculator always appears on launch. (#97)

entries.title: Calculator disguise respects 3-button navigation
entries.description: The bottom row of the disguise calculator could hide behind the navigation bar under 3-button navigation. The buttons now stay clear of the navigation bar in every mode. (#98)

entries.title: Gallery videos play on first open
entries.description: A video opened from the Gallery could show a black screen and only start playing after swiping to another item and back. Videos now begin playing immediately on first open. (#100)

entries.title: Large videos open instantly
entries.description: Opening a big video from the gallery no longer stalls. The player kept re-reading the file from the start on every chunk, so long videos could take a very long time to begin; it now keeps the file open and seeks directly, so they start right away. (#96)

entries.title: Clear message for unplayable videos
entries.description: A video the built-in player can't decode now shows a short message instead of an endless black screen.

entries.title: Play videos with broken frame-rate metadata
entries.description: Some videos declare a nonsensical frame rate that made the built-in player reject them with a black screen, even though they play elsewhere. The player now ignores an implausible declared rate, so these videos play normally. (#104)

entries.title: Refined video player controls
entries.description: Tapping on or near the seek bar no longer hides the player controls by accident, and scrubbing now keeps them on screen and restarts the auto-hide timer. The seek bar itself is slimmer, with a cleaner handle centered on the track.

entries.title: One media viewer everywhere
entries.description: Photos and videos opened from the file browser now use the same full viewer as the Gallery, so you get swipe between items in the folder, EXIF and date editing, rename, delete, export, and the photo editor in both places.

entries.title: Video progress bar updates from the start
entries.description: When opening a video the seek bar stayed at 0:00 and only started moving after tapping it, which also jumped playback back to the beginning. The progress bar and time now advance on their own from the moment the video starts.

entries.title: Screen stays on during video playback
entries.description: The screen no longer dims or turns off while a video is playing, so long videos aren't interrupted by the display timeout. It goes back to the normal timeout as soon as you pause or leave the video. (#105)

entries.title: No auto-lock while media is playing
entries.description: With auto-lock enabled, watching a video or listening to audio counted as idle time, so the vault could lock in the middle of playback. Active playback now keeps the vault unlocked while it plays, and the idle timer resumes the moment you pause. Backgrounding still ages the vault out as before.

entries.title: Shareable crash reports
entries.description: If the app ever crashes, including a native crash that previously left nothing behind, a report is now saved and shown in the debug section so you can copy it and send it along - which makes hard-to-reproduce crashes much easier to track down.

entries.title: No stale mounted state after a background kill
entries.description: If Android closed the app in the background to free memory, a vault could still show as mounted while its files were gone. The app now rechecks on every start, so the vault correctly shows as unmounted and can be remounted with one tap. (#101)

entries.title: Vault storage usage
entries.description: The container's Info tab is now a Storage tab with a breakdown donut showing how much space photos, videos, music, other files, and free space each take up. Tap a category to include or exclude it, or press and hold a slice to peek at its size. General and encryption details moved to a Vault details sheet in vault configuration. (#87)

entries.title: Choose the default vault tab
entries.description: Vaults now open on the Files tab by default instead of the Gallery, so previews of sensitive photos no longer show on unlock. You can switch the default back to Gallery in Appearance settings. (#85)

entries.title: Streamlined What's New
entries.description: The What's New screen now shows the current release up front, with earlier versions tucked behind a Show older versions button for a cleaner view. (#80)

entries.title: Grid view previews and in-app open
entries.description: In the file browser's grid layout, photos and videos now show thumbnails and open inside the app instead of only opening externally - matching the list layout. (#90)

entries.title: Calculator disguise hides PIN lockout
entries.description: After too many wrong PINs the calculator disguise no longer shows a lockout message - a locked-out attempt now looks exactly like a wrong PIN, so the disguise can't be confirmed. The lockout still applies internally. (#88)

entries.title: Tamper-proof PIN lockout timing
entries.description: The PIN lockout can no longer be bypassed by changing the device clock - it uses a monotonic timer with a reboot fallback and stays locked while either clock still says so. (#88)

entries.title: Stronger offline and import hardening
entries.description: Removed a leftover network-state permission so the app requests no network access at all, sanitized folder names during import, and fixed a bounds check when mounting a vault. (#88)

entries.title: Safer password and keyfile changes
entries.description: Changing a vault's password or keyfiles now builds and verifies the new header before removing the old one, so an interrupted or failed change can't leave the vault without a valid header. (#88)

entries.title: Crash confirming with device credential on Android 9-10
entries.description: On Android 9 and 10, enabling the diagnostic logger or turning off screenshot protection crashed the app - the authentication prompt asked for a fingerprint-or-PIN combination the OS rejects on those versions. It now falls back to a supported prompt and can no longer crash. (#92)

entries.title: Auto-lock now counts inactivity
entries.description: Auto-lock triggers after a period of no interaction, not only when the app leaves the foreground - so a vault left open and idle on screen is locked (and unmounted, if set) once the timer runs out. (#60)

entries.title: Open and edit vault files in other apps
entries.description: Turn on External app access for a vault (off by default) and, while it's mounted, other apps can open, edit, create and delete its files straight from the system file picker - no export needed. Nothing is decrypted to disk, and access ends the moment the vault is unmounted. (#55)

entries.title: Share files straight into a vault
entries.description: Turn on Receive shared files in Security (off by default) and Arcanum appears in the Android share sheet, so you can send files from any app straight into a mounted vault - after unlocking and picking the destination folder. While it's off, Arcanum never shows up as a share target. (#93)

entries.title: Stability and data-integrity overhaul
entries.description: An internal audit resolved 27 concurrency, data-loss, and resilience issues across the vault, gallery, file browser, and photo editor: photo saves in the editor are now atomic (a crash during overwrite can no longer corrupt the file), delete operations only update the database when the native delete actually succeeds, vault mount state is fully thread-safe, and a disk error mid-directory-listing now surfaces as a failure instead of silently appearing as an empty folder. (#94)

entries.title: No FAT corruption when writing near a hidden volume
entries.description: When an outer vault was mounted with hidden volume protection enabled, FatFs could allocate a cluster past the hidden boundary, write the FAT chain entry, then fail the data write - leaving the outer volume with a dangling FAT allocation. FatFs's allocator is now capped to the usable outer area and can never place a cluster in the hidden region - while still reading the filesystem exactly as formatted. (#51)

entries.title: Hardened native crypto layer
entries.description: Passwords are now passed as wipeable buffers and cleared from memory, the native code uses full RAII for deterministic cleanup, and the JNI bridge received an extensive security and thread-safety audit.

entries.title: Stronger read-only mounts
entries.description: Read-only mode is now enforced at the operating-system and block-device level, not just in the UI — a read-only vault cannot be modified even through lower-level access.

entries.title: Panic wipe deletes app-storage vaults
entries.description: Vaults saved through the app storage / file picker were left on disk when a panic wipe ran, even though they vanished from the app. Panic now deletes them reliably — in both per-vault and full-wipe modes.

entries.title: Vault media no longer leaks to other apps
entries.description: During playback, real filenames and decrypted thumbnails could be read by other installed apps and shown on the lock screen. The shared media session now carries only a generic title — your filenames and thumbnails stay inside the app.

entries.title: Hidden volume protection when expanding
entries.description: Expanding a vault now guards against overwriting a hidden volume that may exist inside it, preventing accidental destruction of hidden data.

entries.title: Gallery
entries.description: A new Gallery tab gives you a timeline view of all photos and videos inside your vaults. Multi-select, swipe between items, and pinch-to-zoom — all without decrypting to disk.

entries.title: Photo editor
entries.description: Edit photos directly inside the vault — crop, rotate, adjust brightness and contrast — without ever writing the decrypted image to external storage.

entries.title: Background audio playback
entries.description: Audio files from your vaults now play in the background with a media notification and playback controls. Lock the screen and keep listening.

entries.title: Media thumbnails in Files tab
entries.description: Photos and videos now show thumbnails directly in the file browser, decoded on demand and cached for smooth scrolling.

entries.title: Read-only mount mode
entries.description: Vaults can now be mounted in read-only mode — useful for viewing sensitive files without any risk of accidental modification.

entries.title: Import folder
entries.description: Import an entire folder into a vault in one tap. The app copies all files recursively, preserving the folder structure.

entries.title: Open existing vault from app storage
entries.description: A new picker lets you select an existing vault file from app storage without knowing its exact path.

entries.title: Gallery stays in sync with file operations
entries.description: Importing or deleting files in the Files tab now automatically refreshes the Gallery — no manual resync needed.

entries.title: SD card container creation hang
entries.description: Creating a container on an external SD card caused the device to freeze, left a 0-byte file, and made deletion freeze the device again. File allocation is now done incrementally with live progress, and failed attempts are cleaned up instantly.

entries.title: Hidden volume detection
entries.description: Mounting an outer volume without hidden volume protection active incorrectly reported a hidden volume present in some configurations.

entries.title: Expand Volume
entries.description: Resize an existing vault to any larger size without recreating it or touching your data. Progress runs as a foreground service — you can leave the screen and come back.

entries.title: Change Password & Keyfiles
entries.description: Change your vault password or swap keyfiles at any time from the vault configuration screen. A guided wizard re-encrypts only the volume header — your data is never re-written.

entries.title: Backup & Restore Volume Header
entries.description: Export an encrypted backup of your vault header and restore it later if it ever becomes damaged or corrupted. Fully compatible with VeraCrypt desktop backups.

entries.title: Vault configuration screen
entries.description: Each vault now has a dedicated configuration screen — a single hub for mount/unmount, auto-unmount, change password, change keyfiles, header backup, and expand. Tap any vault to open it.

entries.title: Detailed vault info
entries.description: The Info tab now shows a full breakdown of your vault's encryption parameters: cipher, key size, hash algorithm, PKCS-5 iteration count, VeraCrypt format version, and header modification date.

entries.title: Smarter hash selection when mounting
entries.description: If your vault's hash algorithm is known, Arcanum now passes it as a hint and tries only 1 KDF instead of 5, making the mount significantly faster. The Algorithm dropdown is removed — VeraCrypt always tries all ciphers automatically.

entries.title: Faster wrong-password detection
entries.description: The mount logic was rewritten to match VeraCrypt's internal algorithm exactly — same header scan order, same KDF scheduling, same early-exit conditions. Both header copies are now tried in parallel, so wrong credentials are detected and reported significantly faster.

entries.title: Unmount all vaults on auto-lock
entries.description: A new toggle in Security settings automatically unmounts all open vaults when the app auto-locks. Keeps your data inaccessible while the screen is off.

entries.title: Encrypted app database
entries.description: The internal database storing vault metadata is now encrypted with SQLCipher — vault names, paths, and settings are no longer readable from the device filesystem.

entries.title: Hidden volume creation with outer keyfile
entries.description: Creating a hidden volume inside an outer volume that used a keyfile failed silently and left the hidden volume unusable. The outer keyfile is now correctly applied when writing the hidden volume header.

entries.title: Password manager autofill
entries.description: Password fields now show suggestions from your autofill service (e.g. KeePassDX). Selecting a credential automatically fills the Confirm Password field too.

entries.title: Keyfiles never touch disk
entries.description: Keyfiles are now read directly into memory and never written to the app's cache. Previous builds left a temporary plaintext copy on disk during mounting.

entries.title: Biometric unlock remembers keyfiles
entries.description: Containers protected with a keyfile can now be unlocked with biometrics. If a keyfile is later moved or deleted, a clear error screen guides you back to manual mounting.

entries.title: Biometric credentials auto-update
entries.description: Manually mounting a container with the biometric toggle on now refreshes the saved credentials — useful when changing your password or keyfiles.

entries.title: Hidden volume protection confirmed
entries.description: When mounting an outer volume with hidden volume protection enabled, a confirmation screen now appears to confirm that protection is active.

entries.title: Container creation on 32-bit devices
entries.description: Creating containers on arm32 (armeabi-v7a) devices produced a broken, unreadable container. The XTS encryption layer silently operated as 32-bit due to a type definition issue, corrupting the header.

entries.title: Live mount log
entries.description: Enable in debug settings to watch every cipher and PRF combination tried in real time as your container is being unlocked.

entries.title: Update notifications
entries.description: A banner appears the first time you open the app after an update. Tap it to open the What's New screen.

entries.title: Container rename
entries.description: Rename your containers directly from the container config sheet.

entries.title: Smoother UI
entries.description: Tab switches are now animated, and password fields no longer show IME suggestions for better privacy.

entries.title: Bug fixes
entries.description:
• Containers with a custom PIM now open correctly — the iteration formula didn't match the VeraCrypt spec (#48)
• Keyboard and text cursor now close when tapping the mount button
• Swipe-dismissing the update banner no longer permanently marks it as seen
• Biometric prompt now reappears correctly after the app auto-locks in the background

entries.title: Full VeraCrypt compatibility
entries.description: Open containers created on Windows, macOS, or Linux — no conversion needed. AES, Twofish, Serpent and all cascades supported.

entries.title: All hash algorithms
entries.description: BLAKE2s-256, SHA-512, and Whirlpool — fully compatible with VeraCrypt 1.26+.

entries.title: Hidden volumes
entries.description: Two passwords, two independent datasets. Plausible deniability under coercion — mathematically impossible to prove the hidden volume exists.

entries.title: Keyfile support
entries.description: Add one or more keyfiles as a second authentication factor — required alongside the password to open the vault.

entries.title: PIM support
entries.description: Personal Iterations Multiplier for fine-tuned key derivation strength and unlock time.

entries.title: Panic mode
entries.description: Duress PIN silently wipes vaults, settings, and biometrics — timing-indistinguishable from a normal unlock.

entries.title: Calculator disguise
entries.description: Arcanum looks like a regular calculator app. Your secret PIN is the only way in.

entries.title: Biometric unlock
entries.description: Save vault credentials to the hardware Keystore and unlock with fingerprint.

entries.title: Encrypted gallery
entries.description: Browse photos and videos directly inside mounted vaults without extracting them.

entries.title: File manager
entries.description: Import, export, copy, move, and manage files inside encrypted vaults.

entries.title: Audio player
entries.description: Stream audio from encrypted vaults without writing decrypted copies to disk.

entries.title: AMOLED glass mode
entries.description: Pure-black backgrounds with frosted-glass blur throughout the app.
